claim: Library size: how many LNPs are there?
locus_a: Abstract, verbatim: 'Using this b-mRNA screening platform to simultaneously evaluate 122 LNPs'
locus_b: Conclusions, verbatim: 'We formulated a library of 133 distinct mRNA LNPs, each containing a distinct ionizable lipid.' Supplementary Table 3 lists exactly 133 rows, Index contiguous 1..133, counted from native PDF text.
what_we_emitted: NOTHING EMITTED. Both numbers recorded, neither averaged.
why: A third, independent measurement was taken rather than picking a side: Figure 2's heat-map cell pitch. Borders detected as neutral-dark columns at x=48 and x=530 (481 px of cells); the dominant FFT component is 124 cycles, identical in all five strips, and a +/-2 px sweep of both borders gives 123-125. That EXCLUDES 133 and 134 (8-9 bins away) and puts 122 one column below the range. So 133 were formulated and ~124 were screened; 11 or so LNPs are in Supp Table 3 but not in Figure 2, and the paper never says which or why.

claim: Barcode pool size: 134 barcodes for 133 LNPs
locus_a: Supplementary Table 2 title: 'Final 134 barcode sequences established as suitable for in vivo mRNA LNP screening.'
why: Not resolved. A spare barcode, an uninjected-pool control, or an off-by-one; the paper does not say. Recorded because the b-mRNA normalisation divides by the TOTAL barcode count in each sample, so N enters every value, and N is stated three ways in this paper (200 -> 134 -> 133).

claim: 'D<n>' is read as a chain length
locus_a: Supp Fig 2 draws D4 as dibutyl maleate; the MS arithmetic gives a+b = 8.017 carbons, i.e. 4+4. The token IS the per-chain length here.
locus_b: For 17D9.2 the same arithmetic gives a+b = 18.993 across three independently labelled ions, i.e. 19 total, not 2 x 9.2 = 18.4. And the drawn maleate is UNSYMMETRICAL -- a secondary carbinol ester on one side, a 2-ethylhexyl-type primary ester on the other -- so the two chains cannot be equal, 19 being odd.
why: Trap 1 confirmed live in this paper: a name token is not a chain length. What '.2' denotes is stated nowhere in the article or the SI. Recorded rather than guessed.

claim: Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure 14 plot the same screen
locus_a: Both are captioned 'log(1 + Mean normalized accumulation)' over the same 16 sorted populations and the same two strains.
locus_b: Figure 2's x axis is 'Barcode number' spanning ~124 unlabelled columns; Supp Fig 14's axes are 'Amine or thiol' 1..20 and 'Dialkyl maleate' 4/6.2/8/8i/9.2/18, i.e. exactly the 120 nDm members and NONE of the 13 catalogue reagents.
what_we_emitted: NOTHING EMITTED. Treated as a SCOPE difference, not an error.
why: This is the single most consequential fact for attributability, and it cuts both ways: Supp Fig 14 is what makes the 120-member library attributable at all, and it is also why the 13 benchmarks -- including the three lipids shared with the staged sibling mitchellmj_41555650 -- have no attributable value anywhere in this paper.

locus_a: Results, verbatim: 'we opted to analyze b-mRNA accumulation at a relatively short time following treatment'.
locus_b: No hours are given anywhere in the Results, the Methods or the SI for the screen. Figure 3's validation timepoints ARE given (6 h for NanoLuc, 12 h for flow cytometry).
what_we_emitted: NOTHING EMITTED; timepoint left blank in 05_values.csv.
why: Not a contradiction, an absence; recorded because a corpus row would need it and because the authors' own argument for the short timepoint ('peak mRNA translation occurs relatively late') is the reason the screen is not a transfection readout.

claim: RETRACTED (mine): the printed '18.1x' in Figure 3b disagreed with the figure
locus_a: My first Fig 3b digitiser measured the SM-102/LNP 112 liver separation as 15.2 px -> 6.685x, against the printed 18.1x; ratio of ratios 0.369.
locus_b: After repair the same quantity is 23.18 px -> 18.123x, ratio of ratios 1.0013, px error 0.01.
what_we_emitted: The repaired measurement; the printed statistic is correct.
why: RETIRED by three defects found at the source, not by widening a tolerance: (a) the mask mean had swallowed the 131-px-wide grey axis rule; (b) every colour also matched its own LEGEND swatch, the legend sitting inside the plot box; (c) brown annexed the dark anti-aliased flank of the orange marker it overlaps, giving a second spurious SM-102 blob 1.63 px from LNP 97's centre. Fixes: connected components, winner-take-all nearest-colour assignment, a saturation gate, and a minimum centre separation. The printed check is what caught all three.

claim: RETRACTED (mine): Figure 2's heat map has 118 columns
locus_a: A first version of 06b_count_fig2_columns.py reported 118 columns and printed a verdict sentence asserting the abstract's 122 was 'inside the measurement'.
locus_b: Re-measured at 124 (123-125 over a border sweep) once the panel borders were detected correctly.
why: RETIRED by finding the cause: the border detector took 'the outermost full-height dark column' and anchored the left edge on x=69, a SATURATED PURPLE CELL, because a high-value heat-map cell is darker than the panel's grey border. That is error class 20. Selecting on (saturation < 6 AND value < 200) keeps the border and drops every cell. TWO separate lessons: the colour ramp's floor is WHITE, so the span can never be taken from where colour starts; and my verdict SENTENCE was templated and went on asserting the old conclusion after the number moved -- the second time in this folder that prose lagged its own number.

claim: RETRACTED (mine): '123 and 124 are printed numbers this paper reconciles'
locus_a: An intermediate version of 06b listed CANDIDATES = (122, 123, 124, 133, 134) and reported 'printed_numbers_inside_the_range: [123, 124]'.
locus_b: 123 and 124 are MY OWN probe values. The only library sizes this paper prints are 122 (abstract) and 133 (Conclusions, and Supp Table 3's row count); 134 is a barcode count, not an LNP count.
what_we_emitted: CANDIDATES reduced to the numbers the paper actually prints; the field now reads [].
why: RETIRED by reading the primary source again instead of my own output. Recorded rather than edited away silently, because a reader inheriting 'printed_numbers_inside_the_range: [123, 124]' would have inherited a phantom agreement between the paper and itself. The real result is the opposite and sharper: NONE of the printed numbers falls inside the measured range.

claim: RETRACTED (mine): the dashed diagonal in Figure 3b is the PBS spleen:liver ratio line
locus_a: The Methods say tropism is classified against 'the ratio of spleen:liver luminescence in PBS-treated mice', and Fig 3b draws a dashed diagonal with 'Spleen-tropic' above and 'Liver-tropic' below. If the line were that ratio it would test both axis calibrations at once -- a relationship drawn but never printed.
locus_b: Not measurable. The dashed line's grey is the same grey as the panel's anti-aliased text; a robust column-median fit over the one stretch clear of the legend (29 columns) leaves a residual sd of 40.5 px on a 153 px panel.
what_we_emitted: NOTHING. The check is recorded as attempted and refused.
why: RETIRED as NOT COMPUTABLE at 546 px, not as false. Left in the record so the next reader does not spend the same effort believing it is available.
